segments.he: ״בִּטְנְךָ עֲרֵמַת חִטִּים״ – מָה עֲרֵימַת חִטִּים הַכֹּל נֶהֱנִין מִמֶּנָּה, אַף סַנְהֶדְרִין הַכֹּל נֶהֱנִין מִטַּעֲמֵיהֶן. ״סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים״ – שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ כְּסוּגָה שֶׁל שׁוֹשַׁנִּים לֹא יִפְרְצוּ בָּהֶן פְּרָצוֹת.
segments.en: The phrase «“your belly is like a heap of wheat”» teaches that «just as» with regard to «a heap of wheat, all derive benefit from it, so too,» with regard to the «Sanhedrin, all derive benefit from their explanations» of the Torah. The phrase «“set about with lilies”» is said in praise of the Jewish people, «as they do not breach even a fence» made «of lilies,» since the Jewish people observe both Torah law as well as rabbinic ordinances and decrees.
